title: LLM backend swapplaybook workshop - OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Helion's engineering and security stakeholders through a technical migration playbook from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Covered parity mapping for prompts and responses, cost/latency tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private, telemetry and tracing in Redwood Console, and pilot scope. Action items: send parity spreadsheet, propose pilot config, schedule security deep-dive.
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-20 15:30 UTC | Duration: 58m | Recording: internal-link-placeholder
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Jordan (CTO, Helion), Priya (ML Eng), Marcus (Platform), Sofia (Security)

0:00 Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Samir, AE on the account, and with me is Lena, our systems SE. Quick agenda — parity mapping, demo of the API and Console, then Ops and security Qs.
0:18 Jordan (Helion): Thanks, Samir. We'll jump in — we want concrete steps to replace calls to OpenAI/Anthropic/Together without regressing latency or blowing up cost.
0:28 Lena (Redwood): Absolutely. I'll start with a parity matrix we typically use — matches model flavors, tokenization diffs, common prompt transforms, and response shape. Note, some transcriptions in the doc are approximate — e.g., we map Anthropic "HH" style prompts to Redwood's role-based chat.
0:45 Priya (Helion): When you say "role-based chat" is there automatic conversion for our existing prompts? Our infra pipelines preformat messages differently per vendor.
1:02 Lena: Short answer: yes and no. Our API supports a chat/message schema similar to the big vendors, but you may need small prompt scaffolding changes. We provide hooks and a parity spreadsheet to script the changes.
1:20 Marcus: For throughput — we do batched embedding and generation, around 120 requests/s peak. p95 latency matters for interactive UIs. What have other customers seen migrating to Redwood Dedicated?
1:35 Samir: Customers on Dedicated typically get predictable throughput with lower variability; p95/p99 improves since we control packing and kernel selection. We have a telemetry graph in the Console showing token latency by model variant.
1:50 Jordan: Can you demo the Console trace for a canary rollback? That's central to our risk plan.
2:05 Lena: Sure. Opening Redwood Console... (screen share) — apologies if the microphone picks up the fan, transcription may say "Red wood console" in places. Here is a per-route dashboard, you can see token-level cost, latency histograms, and tracing metadata. If a canary exceeds p95 thresholds we can auto-fallback to a cheaper variant or the hosted tier.
2:40 Priya: When you say "cheaper variant" — is that quantized models or smaller-sized checkpoints?
2:48 Lena: Both. We support running a quantized version in Dedicated, and also routing rules to smaller models for tail latency. Our Optimize suggestions will recommend quant profiles by workload.
3:05 Sofia (Helion): On security — what logs are retained? We need audit logs, SSO, and keys in our KMS.
3:12 Samir: For Private and Dedicated we offer Customer-managed KMS/HSM integration, audit logs export, SAML/SSO and RBAC. We also provide a compliance pack for SOC 2 and ISO — I'll share the redacted docs.
3:30 Sofia: Great. Also need DB masking and retention controls — do you support token-level PII filters?
3:38 Lena: We have configurable redaction hooks and prefix caching policies; note the transcriber may confuse KV cache as "kv cash" but it's KV cache. You can configure pre-send filters too.
4:02 Jordan: Let's talk cost. Our baseline for OpenAI is about $X/token for completions and $Y/token for embeddings — big hit. Can Redwood lower that?
4:18 Samir: Yes, by 2 levers: model selection/quantization and batching/caching. For embeddings we often recommend smaller distillation models; for generation batching and prefix cache reduce per-token compute. I can send modeled cost scenarios.
4:40 Priya: Do you support streaming + function calling like OpenAI? We rely on streaming partial tokens to our UI.
4:47 Lena: Streaming is supported, including chunked partial responses and structured function/tool calling patterns. Some customers keep existing webhooks untouched — we emulate the callback pattern.
5:10 Marcus: For our infra team: what's required to point traffic to Redwood? Is it a simple client lib swap or do we need to rework auth?
5:20 Samir: We provide SDKs and a compatible REST interface. Auth is API-key or token-based; for Private you can have mTLS or VPC peering. Typical migration path is: 1) fill parity spreadsheet, 2) run conftest pilot with synthetic workload, 3) run a small canary in Dedicated or Hosted.
5:45 Jordan: Can you walk through that parity spreadsheet live?
5:50 Lena: Sure — sharing sheet. Columns: vendor_model, vendor_prompt, vendor_response_shape, redwood_model_map, prompt_changes, expected_regressions, test_prompt_id. Example: Together's "together-medium" -> Redwood "rw-medium-v1"; note tokenizers differ so token counts are +/ - a few percent.
6:18 Priya: Are there any known behavior diffs that commonly break our QA? e.g., system instruction handling or stop sequence behaviors.
6:27 Lena: Yes — system instruction semantics and stop sequences. Anthropic long-form safety prompts might need conversion. We add small guardrails and recommend regression sets as part of the pilot.
6:50 Jordan: Ok. Let's go deeper on benchmarks — can you run a tail-latency benchmark for our typical prompt distribution? We have heavy long-context history in chat.
7:02 Samir: We'll do an internal benchmark with your prompts. Actionable plan: Redwood runs 1k requests with your prompt corpus across model variants: hosted, dedicated quant, dedicated fp16. Then provide token cost delta and p95/p99 comparisons.
7:22 Marcus: Timeline for that?
7:25 Samir: If you share the prompt set this week, we can return initial numbers in 5 business days.
7:30 Priya: A note — some of our pipelines assume OpenAI's exact error shapes; how do you handle error codes?
7:38 Lena: We try to be compatible but we expose more granular error codes in some cases; we'll provide an adapter layer in the SDK. The SDK also includes transcripts or response metadata so you can map errors.
7:55 Jordan: Any customers who did a full switch recently you can reference?
8:00 Samir: Yes — mid-market analytics customer (anonymous) migrated from a multi-vendor stack to Dedicated and saw 20% lower per-token cost after quantization and 30% fewer latency spikes. I'll share the case study.
8:18 Sofia: For legal we need data residency controls — can you pin region?
8:25 Samir: Yes, Dedicated and Private allow region pinning and VPC controls. Hosted API has region hints but less determinism.
8:40 Priya: Demo time — can we do a quick API parity call? I want to see request/response shapes for messages -> streaming.
8:48 Lena: Doing a live curl example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"rw-chat-v1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize X"}] }'
9:12 Priya: Looks similar. Will our telemetry correlators pick up token ids and request ids?
9:20 Lena: Yes, we include request_id and token_level timing if you enable advanced tracing. Note: the console may display truncated traces in the demo due to sampling.
9:40 Marcus: What about function calling? Any differences in payloads?
9:46 Lena: We support structured function calling patterns. The JSON schema is essentially the same; some naming differs. We'll include a migration snippet in the parity sheet.
10:05 Jordan: Ok let's discuss pilot scope — we want minimal blast radius and measurable KPIs.
10:12 Samir: Proposed pilot: 2 models (generation and embeddings), 2 routes, 2 weeks. KPIs: p95 latency within X% of current, token cost delta, and call success rate > 99.5%.
10:28 Priya: For embeddings, can we do a side-by-side with our current vector db pipeline? We need vector similarity parity.
10:36 Lena: Yes. We can produce embeddings and run recall tests versus your current db. Also include dimensionality and normalization diffs in the parity doc.
10:52 Jordan: Anything about fallback patterns? If Dedicated is full do we failover to Hosted or to a smaller model?
11:00 Samir: We support smart routing: fallback to hosted, or to encoded smaller model variant, or to queued requests depending on policy. You control SLO thresholds per route.
11:18 Sofia: Security follow-up — can you send the encryption in transit docs and SOC 2 details? We'll want to kick off a security review with our compliance team.
11:28 Samir: Yes, will send. Also, for Private deployments we can run on-prem packages; that'll be a separate engagement.
11:40 Priya: Gotcha. Any gotchas when converting Together prompts? We use some of their system prompt wrappers.
11:48 Lena: Together's tokenization and system prefixing can change generation probabilities; recommend running golden regression tests. The parity sheet has a flag for "likely rewrite needed".
12:05 Jordan: Let's highlight actionable next steps before we wrap.
12:10 Samir: Recap: 1) Helion shares anonymized prompt corpus and traffic profile; 2) Redwood runs benchmark and returns cost/latency matrix; 3) We share parity spreadsheet and migration snippets; 4) Schedule security deep-dive with Sofia and Compliance; 5) Agree pilot start date.
12:35 Marcus: Does Redwood provide a test harness for synthetic load?
12:42 Lena: Yes — we can provide a small k8s-based harness or run it for you in our test environment.
12:55 Priya: About monitoring: do you expose Prometheus metrics or is it Console-only?
13:02 Lena: We export metrics to Prometheus/Grafana and also provide the Console. Customers usually ingest both.
13:20 Jordan: Great. That's super helpful. Let's plan on sharing the prompt set by Friday.
13:30 Samir: Sounds good. I'll email the parity sheet and the initial checklist after this call. Thanks everyone.
13:40 (end recording)
